name: Chip supply
value: TSMC halts some China orders at 16nm and below
summary: New US rules from 19 Nov led TSMC to halt some Chinese orders at 16nm and below; Samsung said to pause some shipments
state: New US Commerce Department rules effective 19 Nov removed a compliance route that let some Chinese chip designers use advanced foundry services without licences, and TSMC has suspended orders at 16nm and below unless customers obtain US licences (The Standard; Taipei Times). The Financial Times reported that Samsung also paused some shipments to Chinese customers. This follows US licence rules from 16 Nov for AI chips to five countries. New controls keep Watch; TSMC and Samsung output itself is not disrupted.
for_you: Chinese chip designers and their customers are most exposed. Wider electronics supply is not disrupted. Further US or Chinese counter-measures tend to follow such rules within weeks.
rubric_hit: Watch: new export controls (US rule of 19 Nov; TSMC halts some sub-16nm China orders); no TSMC/Samsung output disruption

sources.title: The Standard — TSMC tightens China AI chip curbs as new US rules close manufacturing loophole
Taipei Times — TSMC tightens restrictions on Chinese chip designers

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
